models.name: discussion_board_platform_configurations
models.description:
Platform-wide configuration settings and system parameters that control the behavior of the discussion board service.

This table stores key-value configuration pairs that define how the economic and political discussion platform operates globally. Configurations include settings for article limits, attachment sizes, notification preferences, moderation policies, and other system-wide parameters that influence platform behavior.

Configuration entries are referenced by system components but not directly queried by users. Changes to configurations require administrative approval and may trigger platform-wide updates for immediate or delayed application.

The configuration system supports different data types (strings, numbers, booleans) stored as string values with appropriate parsing when retrieved, allowing flexible system administration without database migrations for new settings.

Soft deletion is supported to maintain audit trails when configuration values change over time.

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Configuration key identifier, used to lookup specific settings throughout the platform.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Configuration value content, stored as string but may represent different data types when interpreted.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description explaining the purpose and format of this configuration setting.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the configuration, either active for live use or inactive for deprecated settings.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was initially created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for audit trails, allowing recovery of historical configurations.

models.name: discussion_board_categories
models.description:
Primary categorization system for organizing economic and political discussion content within the platform.

Categories represent the top-level organizational structure that users interact with directly when creating and browsing articles. They provide clear segmentation between economic topics (finance, markets, policy) and political topics (legislation, international relations, current events), helping users find relevant content and encouraging focused discussions.

Categories are prominently displayed in navigation menus and search filters, serving as primary entry points for content discovery. Each category can contain multiple sections for further subdivision while maintaining meaningful boundaries.

Category definitions include display names, descriptions, and unique codes for internationalization support. Status management allows for seasonal or contextual category activation/deactivation without data loss.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Display name of the category for user interface presentation.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description explaining the category's scope and what type of content belongs here.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Unique identifier code used for URL routing and internationalization key mapping.

plainFields.name: order
plainFields.description: Display ordering for navigation menus, with lower numbers appearing first.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current operational status of the category, either active for user access or inactive for archival.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this category was initially created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this category was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for archival categories that are no longer active.

models.name: discussion_board_sections
models.description:
Subsidiary organizational units that provide finer-grained grouping within discussion categories.

Sections exist to support the primary categorization system by allowing sub-divisions within broader topics. For example, an 'Economy' category might contain sections for 'Stock Markets', 'Cryptocurrency', 'Fiscal Policy', and 'Labor Markets', enabling users to dive deeper into specific sub-topics while still maintaining connection to the parent category.

Sections are managed through their parent categories and provide additional search and filtering granularity. They help balance between having too few broad categories and too many unwieldy small ones, improving content discoverability.

While sections are subsidiary to categories, they still require unique identification for proper referencing by articles and maintaining consistent organization throughout discussion threads.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Display name of the section for user interface presentation.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description explaining the section's scope and content boundaries.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Unique identifier code within the parent category for URL routing and reference.

plainFields.name: order
plainFields.description: Display ordering within the parent category, with lower numbers appearing first.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current operational status of the section, either active or inactive.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this section was initially created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this section was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for archival sections that are no longer active.

models.name: discussion_board_guests
models.description:
Anonymous visitors who browse and view public articles and discussions without requiring authentication or account creation.

Guests represent the primary audience for the discussion board content, consuming economic and political analysis through articles and threaded comments. They provide implicit feedback through browsing patterns and serve as potential conversion points to member registration.

While guests cannot create content or participate in discussions, their access patterns help inform content strategy and platform optimization for the economic discussion community.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest first accessed the platform.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last access or activity.

models.name: discussion_board_members
models.description:
Registered users who can actively participate in discussions by creating articles, posting comments, and managing their contributions to the economic and political discourse.

Members create the primary content for the discussion board, sharing their insights through comprehensive articles supported by image and file attachments. They engage in threaded discussions, report inappropriate content, and build community reputation through quality contributions.

All members must verify their email address before gaining full publishing capabilities, ensuring a baseline of account authenticity for the serious content standards of the platform.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Email address used for registration, password reset, and platform notifications. Must be unique and verified before article publishing.

plainFields.name: username
plainFields.description: Unique username for public display in articles and comments. Follows platform naming conventions.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for secure authentication. Generated from user-provided password during registration.

plainFields.name: email_verified_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when email verification was completed, null until verified.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last account update or activity.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for account deactivation.

models.name: discussion_board_member_sessions
models.description:
Session records for authenticated member logins, tracking access patterns and supporting account security for discussion board members.

Each member login creates a session record that maintains authentication state across browser refreshes and page navigation. Sessions expire after 30 days of inactivity to ensure continuous security for the economic and political discussion platform.

Session tracking enables activity monitoring, security enforcement, and helps identify authorized access patterns during content creation and discussion participation.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged member who initiated this session. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the connection.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL where the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL for tracking session origin.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration timestamp.

models.name: discussion_board_admins
models.description:
Privileged users responsible for system governance, content moderation, and user management to ensure the discussion board operates effectively and safely.

Administrators maintain platform quality and enforce community standards for economic and political discourse through comprehensive moderation powers. They review flagged content, manage user accounts, and access advanced analytics to support healthy community growth.

Admin accounts follow the same registration pattern as members but include enhanced permissions for moderation, user management, and system configuration access.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Email address used for registration, password reset, and admin notifications. Must be unique and verified.

plainFields.name: username
plainFields.description: Unique username for admin display in moderation logs. Follows platform naming conventions.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for secure admin authentication. Generated from user-provided password.

plainFields.name: email_verified_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when email verification was completed, null until verified.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the admin account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last admin activity or account update.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for admin account deactivation.

models.name: discussion_board_admin_sessions
models.description:
Session records for authenticated admin logins, tracking access patterns and supporting enhanced security for administrative system access.

Each admin login creates a privileged session that enables content moderation, user management, and system configuration. Sessions expire after 30 days of inactivity to protect sensitive administrative functions.

Session tracking provides audit trails for administrative actions, security monitoring for privileged access, and supports secure management operations within the economic and political discussion platform.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged admin who initiated this session. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the admin connection.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL where the admin session was initiated.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL for tracking admin session origin.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration timestamp.

models.name: discussion_board_articles
models.description:
Main article entities containing user-created content on economic and political topics.

This table stores the core article data including titles, content, and metadata. Articles serve as the primary content units that users create to share analysis and opinions on economic trends and political events, forming the foundation of the discussion ecosystem.

Each article is authored by a registered member and can be organized into categories for topic organization. The table supports the complete article lifecycle with rich text content and file attachments support.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member who authored the article. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_category_id
foreignFields.description: Category classification for the article. {@link discussion_board_categories.id}

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Article title for clear topic identification.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Article main content in rich text format.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Unique business identifier for stable referencing.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Publication status of the article. Valid values: draft, published.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Article creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last modification timestamp.

models.name: discussion_board_article_snapshots
models.description:
Historical snapshots of article states for audit trails and change tracking.

This table captures point-in-time versions of articles whenever they are modified, preserving the complete state including title, content, category assignments, and all associated metadata for transparency in content evolution.

Snapshots are created automatically during edits, maintaining an immutable record of changes that supports moderation and historical analysis of economic and political discussions.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Snapshot of article title at point in time.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Snapshot of article content at point in time.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Business identifier as in snapshot.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Original article creation time.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Snapshot creation timestamp.

models.name: discussion_board_article_attachments
models.description:
Supporting files attached to articles for comprehensive content presentation.

This table manages file attachments that accompany articles, storing metadata about uploaded files while keeping actual files in separate storage for scalability.

Attachments are subsidiary to articles and include various file types as specified in requirements, supporting the enrichment of economic and political analyses with documents and media.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Original file name for user identification.

plainFields.name: uri
plainFields.description: Secure access URI for file downloading.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: File MIME type for proper handling.

plainFields.name: size
plainFields.description: File size in bytes for display.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Attachment upload timestamp.

models.name: discussion_board_comments
models.description:
Primary discussion entities for threaded conversations on articles.

This table stores user comments and replies that form the discussion ecosystem beneath articles, enabling structured dialogue on economic and political topics.

Comments are authored by members and can form threaded reply structures, supporting nested conversations with optional attachments for comprehensive discussion contributions.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Article this comment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

foreignFields.name: parent_discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Parent comment for reply threading. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Comment text content.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Comment creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last modification timestamp.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_snapshots
models.description:
Historical snapshots of comment states for change tracking in discussions.

This table captures point-in-time versions of comments during edits, preserving content evolution and supporting moderation of threaded conversations.

Snapshots maintain the integrity of discussion threads by tracking changes to individual comments and their reply structures within the economic and political discourse.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Snapshot of comment content at point in time.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Original comment creation time.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Snapshot creation timestamp.

Supporting files attached to comments for enhanced discussion contributions.

This table manages file attachments that accompany individual comments, storing metadata for uploaded files while enabling richer discussion interactions.

Comment attachments are subsidiary to comments and support the same file types as article attachments, allowing members to include relevant documents in their discussion points.
